YouTube](http://img.shields.io/badge/youtube-nf--core-FF0000?labelColor=000000&logo=youtube)](https://www.youtube.com/c/nf-core) ## Introduction **nf-core/evefinder** finds Endogenous Viral Elements (EVEs) in eukaryotic genomes with [EEfinder](https://github.com/WallauBioinfo/EEfinder), running every `eefinder screening` stage as its own process, one genome at a time. The pipeline has three steps (`--step`): 1. `prepare_inputs`: downloads each genome (NCBI Datasets API, FASTA + GFF3, or ENA browser API, FASTA), the host protein baits (`eefinder get-databases host`, taxon taken from the genome) and, optionally, the viral protein database (`eefinder get-databases virus`), both indexed for `--search_mode`, and writes the samplesheet for `screening`. 2. `screening`: validates each database/metadata/baits set (`eefinder screening prepare`, which reuses the indexes beside the FASTAs and builds the missing ones), then runs `eefinder screening clean → align → filter → taxonomy → merge → postprocess → flanks` per genome, publishing `PREFIX.EEs.{fa,tax.tsv,gff3,faa,flanks.fa}` (the GFF3 with the CDS of each element, and their proteins), and clusters each genome's elements (cd-hit-est or vclust). 3. `analysis`: reads a finished screening and builds the genome phylogeny (mashtree) and the plots: an interactive HTML of the tree beside the elements per genome and taxon, and a Krona chart and a swarm plot per genome. ## Usage > [!NOTE] > If you are new to Nextflow and nf-core, please refer to [this page](https://nf-co.re/docs/get_started/environment_setup/overview) on how to set-up Nextflow. Make sure to [test your setup](https://nf-co.re/docs/get_started/run-your-first-pipeline) with `-profile test` before running the workflow on actual data. First, list the genomes (`virus_taxid` is optional: one viral database is downloaded per distinct value, and rows without one use EEfinder's default, 10239): ```csv accession,virus_taxid GCA_021653915.1,11050 GCF_000146045.2, ``` ```yaml title="prepare.yml" step: prepare_inputs input: genomes.csv download_virus_db: true virus_db_release_date: "2026-01-01" outdir: results ``` ```bash nextflow run nf-core/evefinder -profile docker -params-file prepare.yml ``` Set `virus_db_fasta`/`virus_db_metadata` instead of `download_virus_db` to use a local database, and `genome_source: ena` to download from ENA. Boolean and integer parameters go in the `-params-file`: from Nextflow 26.04 on, command-line parameters always arrive as strings, so they fail validation (`--download_virus_db true`, `--min_length 1000`). Then screen the genomes with the samplesheet it wrote: ```bash nextflow run nf-core/evefinder -profile docker \ --step screening \ --input /prepare_inputs/samplesheet.csv \ --outdir ``` Then analyse the screening, with the same samplesheet: ```bash nextflow run nf-core/evefinder -profile docker \ --step analysis \ --input /prepare_inputs/samplesheet.csv \ --screening_outdir \ --outdir ``` The `screening` samplesheet has the columns `sample,taxid,genome,baits,db_fasta,db_metadata`, so it can also be written by hand. Every `eefinder get-databases` and `eefinder screening` option is a pipeline parameter (see `nextflow_schema.json`). > [!WARNING] > Please provide pipeline parameters via the CLI or Nextflow `-params-file` option. Custom config files including those provided by the `-c` Nextflow option can be used to provide any configuration _**except for parameters**_; see [docs](https://nf-co.re/docs/running/run-pipelines#using-parameter-files). ### Running on a single machine The `local` profile (`conf/local.config`) caps what tasks may request at what one machine has (16 CPUs, 18 GB, 48 h; edit it to match yours). Without it, the `process_high` label asks for 72 GB and the run stops on a laptop. Combine it with a container engine: **Docker** (macOS, Linux): ```bash nextflow run nf-core/evefinder -profile local,docker -params-file prepare.yml nextflow run nf-core/evefinder -profile local,docker --step screening --input results/prepare_inputs/samplesheet.csv --outdir results ``` - On macOS the tasks run inside a Linux VM (Docker Desktop or Colima), so the VM's limits are what counts: `conf/local.config` follows them, not the Mac's. Raise them in Docker Desktop's Settings > Resources, or with `colima stop && colima start --cpu 16 --memory 20`, then edit `conf/local.config` to match. - The EEfinder image (`dezordi/eefinder:2.0.0-dev`) is not on Docker Hub yet: build it from the EEfinder checkout with `docker build --platform linux/amd64 -t dezordi/eefinder:2.0.0-dev .`. Singularity/Apptainer cannot pull it until it is pushed. It is `linux/amd64` only; on Apple Silicon it runs through emulation (Rosetta), with a platform warning in the task logs. - The VM only mounts shared folders (`/Users` in Docker Desktop, your home directory in Colima by default): launch from, and write `--outdir`/`-work-dir` to, a path under one of them, not `/tmp`. **Singularity / Apptainer** (Linux, HPC): ```bash nextflow run nf-core/evefinder -profile local,singularity -params-file prepare.yml nextflow run nf-core/evefinder -profile local,apptainer --step screening --input results/prepare_inputs/samplesheet.csv --outdir results ``` - The images are pulled from Docker Hub/quay.io and converted on first use; set `NXF_SINGULARITY_CACHEDIR` (or `NXF_APPTAINER_CACHEDIR`) to reuse them across runs. - On a cluster, drop `local` and use your institution's profile (`-profile ,singularity`), which sets the scheduler and its limits. Check the setup with the test profile first (`-profile test,local,docker`): it screens an _Aedes aegypti_ contig, whose outputs match EEfinder's own golden files, and two genomes without elements. `-profile test_analysis,local,docker` on the same `--outdir` then builds the tree of the three genomes and the plots. For more details and further functionality, please refer to the [usage documentation](https://nf-co.re/evefinder/usage) and the [parameter documentation](https://nf-co.re/evefinder/parameters). ## Pipeline output To see the results of an example test run with a full size dataset refer to the [results](https://nf-co.re/evefinder/results) tab on the nf-core website pipeline page. For more details about the output files and reports, please refer to the [output documentation](https://nf-co.re/evefinder/output). ## Credits nf-core/evefinder was originally written by [Filipe Dezordi](https://orcid.org/0000-0003-3259-3456) and [Yago José Mariz Dias](https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0786-6435). ## Contributions and Support If you would like to contribute to this pipeline, please see the [contributing guidelines](docs/CONTRIBUTING.md). For further information or help, don't hesitate to get in touch on the [Slack `#evefinder` channel](https://nfcore.slack.com/channels/evefinder) (you can join with [this invite](https://nf-co.re/join/slack)). ## Citations An extensive list of references for the tools used by the pipeline can be found in the [`CITATIONS.md`](CITATIONS.md) file. You can cite the `nf-core` publication as follows: > **The nf-core framework for community-curated bioinformatics pipelines.** > > Philip Ewels, Alexander Peltzer, Sven Fillinger, Harshil Patel, Johannes Alneberg, Andreas Wilm, Maxime Ulysse Garcia, Paolo Di Tommaso & Sven Nahnsen. > > _Nat Biotechnol._ 2020 Feb 13. doi: [10.1038/s41587-020-0439-x](https://dx.doi.org/10.1038/s41587-020-0439-x).
